questions.question: How did the first steamships move, and why were they better than sailing ships?
questions.expected_answer: Steam engines burned coal and turned paddle wheels, and later propellers, which pushed the ship through the water. They were better because they did not need the wind, so they could keep to a timetable and journeys were faster and more reliable.

questions.question: How did steamships change South Africa's links with the world?
questions.expected_answer: Mail ships, such as those of the Union-Castle Line, carried letters, passengers and goods between Britain and South Africa every week, and the journey took about two weeks instead of months. Harbours were made bigger and railways were built from the harbours to the mines and cities.

questions.question: Name three kinds of ships used today and what each one carries.
questions.expected_answer: Container ships carry goods in large metal containers. Bulk carriers carry loose goods such as coal, iron ore and grain. Tankers carry oil and fuel. Ferries carry people and vehicles, cruise ships carry tourists, and fishing boats catch fish.
